class.name: Vst3SidechainSend
class.brief_description: Sends a bus's audio to the sidechain input of Vst3PluginEffect plugins.
class.description:
Put this on the bus whose sound should drive a plugin's sidechain: a ducking compressor's key input, or a vocoder's carrier, for example. It passes its bus through unchanged, and copies each block of audio into the channel named [member channel]. Any [Vst3PluginEffect] whose [member Vst3PluginEffect.sidechain] has the same name then hears it on its second input. [codeblock] var send = Vst3SidechainSend.new() send.channel = "kick" AudioServer.add_bus_effect(AudioServer.get_bus_index("Drums"), send)
compressor.sidechain = "kick" # A Vst3PluginEffect on another bus. [/codeblock] When the source bus falls silent and Godot stops processing it, the sidechain falls silent too. [b]Note:[/b] Godot processes buses from the highest index down. If this send's bus has a higher index than the plugin's bus, the plugin hears the same audio block; otherwise one block (about 11.6 ms at 44.1 kHz) later. VST is a registered trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH. [b]Note:[/b] Only [Vst3PluginEffect] effects hear this send. A bus that drives both formats needs a Vst3SidechainSend and a ClapSidechainSend, each with the channel name. [b]Note:[/b] On a surround bus, only the front left and right channels are sent. Use one send per channel name: the same send on two buses would mix two buses' blocks into one channel.

members.member: The channel's name, matched against [member Vst3PluginEffect.sidechain]. Changing it applies at once, to running instances too. Empty sends nothing.
